public_payload.normalized_proposition: After the June 2025 priority tiers, nearly every AI startup had to institute austerity.

statement.excerpt: Over the next few months, just about every AI startup had to institute some form of austerity.
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

our_interpretation: In context, austerity means price increases, tighter included-usage limits, reduced services, or other spending cuts intended to contain costs.
The relevant population is AI startups selling applications or model services, rather than all businesses that use AI.
The period runs from June 2025 through March 2026 because the surrounding examples extend from June changes to February and current March developments.
Just about every means nearly all, not merely several prominent examples. No arbitrary numerical cutoff is added.
Had to adds a necessity claim that requires evidence beyond observing a pricing change.
criteria.support_condition: A representative record shows cost-containment measures at nearly all relevant AI startups during the target period, with evidence that economic or capacity pressures required them.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows a substantial share of relevant startups did not institute such measures, or that the changes attributed to necessary austerity were predominantly unrelated commercial changes.
